turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
You gave Owen a zero before anyone picked up a phone. On what basis?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Owen's mother will do. You still haven't told me the basis.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
Times with nothing under them. Show me the document, and tell me whether Owen was asked about it before you entered the zero.
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
This isn't a courtroom, Hale, and it isn't funny. The document.
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
A misquoted line makes a seventeen-year-old careless, nothing more. Put the essay in front of me.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
Different writer. Or a kid who changed his mind in two weeks, which is what drafting is for. You've described three things now and shown me none of them.
And the school checker says 94%.
There it is. A machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in writing not to punish a student on it alone; I have that page in my bag. Your own 4.3 says the same.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Save it. Show me something with a date on it.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
Nobody's stepping anywhere. Owen's essay.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
I'm not here to teach you your job, Hale. I'm here for my son, and the zero is still sitting there.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? Owen.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
You were about to show me a document. And tell me why nobody called me before that zero went in.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
Nothing on his record, in writing, is 4.4, and I'll hold you to every word. But a rewrite for what, Hale? You still haven't shown me a thing.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
A deadline isn't evidence. Pull it tomorrow and you can explain why to the principal.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
I don't prove anything to you. You prove it to me, and you still haven't.
